endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: This can be assessed using such metrics as percentage of draft retained, incorrect content, and bespoke quality of documentation analyses developed by vendors or health systems.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this recommendation tests whether tracking ambient scribe opt-out rates detects patient discomfort or consent problems, and no study documents the hazard itself. One guidance document offers permissive support, and its quoted text describes documentation quality metrics rather than opt-out rates.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero that document the hazard. The single endorsement is guidance worded as "may," and its quoted passage names draft retention, incorrect content, and quality analyses, which do not include opt-out percentage. Certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that measure ambient scribe opt-out rates across clinics and compare them with direct measures of patient discomfort and consent quality, such as post-visit surveys or consent audits. Such studies would show whether opt-out rates are a valid signal, what baseline and threshold values mean, and whether low opt-out rates reflect comfort or patients' reluctance to decline.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations, because no study was supplied. Opt-out rates may understate discomfort in groups who face language or literacy barriers to understanding or refusing recording, so any monitoring program would need its own validation in those populations.
